title: PostgreSQL Performance: Local vs. Network-Attached Storage
summary: Cloud storage was built around the limits of old hardware. With NVMe SSDs being faster, cheaper, and more reliable, it's time to rethink PostgreSQL storage.
body_text: PostgreSQL Performance: Local vs. Network-Attached Storage May 30, 2025 · 3 min read Burak Yucesoy Principal Software Engineer Cloud storage was built around the limits of old hardware. Spinning hard drives (HDDs) were slow and fragile. So, early on cloud providers moved storage off of servers. They used network-attached disks to boost durability and scalability. But hardware has come a long way. Modern NVMe SSDs have eliminated many of the constraints that originally led to network-attached designs. They are also much more affordable. You can get 2.5 million IOPS from a $600 NVMe SSD [ 1 ]. By contrast, pushing 2.5 million IOPS through Aurora would cost you $1.3M per month. With NVMe SSDs being faster, cheaper, and more reliable, it's time to rethink PostgreSQL storage. In this post, we’ll explore how cloud database storage architectures have evolved, how advances in hardware have changed the landscape, and why local NVMe SSDs have become a viable option for cloud databases. We’ll also present benchmarks that compare performance across different storage architectures. Database Storage over the Years Before the cloud, databases typically ran on local hard drives (HDDs). This provided low latency for sequential reads but introduced two challenges. Each HDD had a single head sitting on a platter, so your random read/write performance would be terrible. These HDDs also had high annual failure rates due to rotating disks. Most database teams would buy specialized hard drives and put them into fancy RAID configurations to compensate for these problems. Then, cloud computing happened. AWS made a bold move and popularized pooling storage remotely across many machines. They connected servers to big clusters of HDDs over a network, solving two major issues at once. There were no bottlenecks due to single disk as you could spread I/O over many drives. It also provided higher redundancy and durability by replicating data in the background. At the time, database engineers worried that the extra network hop would kill performance. Surprisingly, it worked well enough and network-attached storage became the default for cloud databases. With SSDs, trade-offs in cloud architecture have fundamentally changed. Fast speed: SSDs offer high throughput and low latency. This removes much of the performance advantage of spreading I/O across many drives. No moving parts: SSDs are much more reliable than HDDs. This has reduced the durability advantage that centralized storage used to offer. Falling prices: High-performance storage is now affordable. This makes SSDs a cost-effective option for intensive tasks. Over time, SSDs became more popular due to their better performance, reliability and falling prices. So, cloud providers upgraded their network-attached storage to use SSDs. However, the fundamental design, storage accessed over the network, remained unchanged. This was partly due to path dependency and partly because network-attached storage still offers advantages in certain areas, which we’ll discuss the in next section. The advancements in SSD technology continued even further with NVMe SSDs. Traditional SSDs often used SATA or SAS interfaces, originally designed for spinning disks. In contrast, NVMe was built specifically for flash memory. It connects directly over PCIe, enabling massively parallel data paths and reducing latency. As we mentioned in the beginning, the cost of 2.5 million IOPS on Aurora is $1.3M/month, but you can achieve the same performance with a $600 local NVMe SSD. Yet cloud providers stuck with network-attached storage, largely out of inertia. At Ubicloud, we believe it’s time for a reset. Advantages of Network-Attached Storage Local NVMe SSDs deliver major performance benefits. However, network-attached storage still has two key advantages: elasticity and durability. Elasticity allows you to scale storage independently of compute. This is especially useful for unpredictable workloads with fluctuating storage needs. In contrast, local storage is coupled with the underlying compute. Scaling it often requires moving data to a new server with larger disks. It is possible to automate this process and perform it safely, but definitely adds some operational complexity. Durability is another strength of network-attached storage. Centralized network storage systems are usually highly durable due to their built-in replication. That said, NVMe SSDs are already far more reliable than legacy HDDs. This minimizes the risk of disk failure. Still, when using local NVMe, it's important to have a replication and backup strategy in place. Thankfully, PostgreSQL already comes with robust primitives for replication, high availability, and backups. So, building a resilient system for PostgreSQL on top of local NVMe is entirely feasible. In summary, network-attached storage offers certain operational advantages, but modern hardware, automation and database tooling make local NVMe a compelling choice in many scenarios. At Ubicloud, this is why we’re confident in using local NVMe for our managed PostgreSQL service. Next up Quick Start - Build your own cloud Benchmarks We wanted to know how much better PostgreSQL could be with local NVMe drives, so we ran performance benchmarks across three platforms: Ubicloud PostgreSQL: standard-8 instance (comes with 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM and local NVMe SSD) Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: db.m8g.2xlarge instance (comes with 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM) and GP3 EBS disk Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL: db.r8g.2xlarge instance (comes with 8 vCPU, 64GB RAM) and I/O optimized disk. To evaluate performance, we ran two industry-standard benchmarks: TPC-C : This benchmark emulates OLTP workloads, characterized by high concurrency and small transactions. We used sysbench to run TPC-C benchmark (tables: 32, scale: 256) TPC-H : This benchmark emulates analytical workloads, characterized by large scans and complex joins. We used 100 as the scale factor. On the TPC-C benchmark, Ubicloud with NVMe drives processes 1.4 times more queries than Aurora and 4.6 times more queries than RDS. Latency at 99th percentile was 1.9 times less compared to Aurora and 7.7 times less than RDS. Workload Ubicloud Aurora RDS Transaction/s 873.25 636.31 188.3 Query/s 24815.08 18076.31 5350.79 Latency 314.45 601.29 2405.65 Drag table left or right to see remaining content Moreover, latency was more stable and predictable with NVMe drives. On the TPC-H benchmark, Ubicloud with NVMe drives were faster in all TPC-H queries. On average, it was 2.42 times faster than Aurora and 2.96 times faster than RDS. Ubicloud Aurora RDS Q01 75.4 170.4 174.8 Q02 108.65 238.86 129.69 Q03 60.95 101.4 223.59 Q04 119.65 552.57 355.73 Q05 63.19 83.69 223.53 Q06 45.91 61.42 179.26 Q07 60.96 76.28 223.72 Q08 69.92 92.86 254.33 Q09 84.94 1596.24 275.71 Q10 91.38 123.96 314.85 Q11 35.29 76.76 102.38 Q12 65.72 119.75 240.15 Q13 48.66 80.44 83.23 Q14 46.74 74.11 181.5 Q15 97.94 161.96 365.75 Q16 100.05 107.41 107.35 Q17 235.25 542.08 559.31 Q18 225.73 605.84 2142.52 Q19 23.17 161.77 111.9 Q20 1825.97 10666.92 9866.06 Q21 103.87 729.29 213.65 Q22 9.88 30.37 10.49 Mean (Geometric) 79.72 193.23 235.61 Difference - 2.42x 2.96x Drag table left or right to see remaining content The Future of Cloud Databases Is Local We’re at an inflection point. The cloud storage model built 15 years ago no longer makes sense for today’s hardware and workloads. For data intensive applications like PostgreSQL, local SSDs are the better default.

title: Metadata and Reproducibility
summary: Enhancing FAIR Data Workflows through use of PIDs in Curvenote and beyond.
body_text: Metadata and Reproducibility Tactics to improve informal research communication Rowan Cockett · June 23, 2022 Curvenote participated in a BoF session on building enhanced FAIR Workflows through use of PIDs within and between interoperable research tools. Abstract - RDA Website ¶ The lack of interoperability between tools presents a significant barrier to streamlining workflows throughout the research lifecycle. These gaps prevent the comprehensive collection and incorporation of research data and metadata into the research record captured during the active research phase. Furthermore, it limits the scope for passing this data and metadata on to data repositories, thus undermining FAIR data principles and reproducibility. "This session will explore several use cases of how tools are utilizing the passage of PIDs between systems as a means to build streamlined, FAIR workflows. Moving from theory to implementation involves many moving parts. The panel session explores issues, highlights existing integrations, and points to possible ways forward. Curvenote Presentation ¶ As a part of this presentation we improved our support in Curvenote for RRIDs & RORs, which we will share more about soon! 🚀 Figure 1: Using RRIDs in Curvenote.

Great Southern Bank Partners with Greenlight
summary: Great Southern Bank today announced a partnership with Greenlight® Financial Technology, Inc. (“Greenlight”) to better serve families across its footprint and help the next generation build healthy financial futures.
body_text: Springfield, MO — Great Southern Bank today announced a partnership with Greenlight® Financial Technology, Inc. (“Greenlight”) to better serve families across its footprint and help the next generation build healthy financial futures. Beginning today, Great Southern customers have free* access to Greenlight’s award-winning family finance app through the Greenlight for Banks program. The need for accessible financial education has never been greater. Ninety-one percent of kids and teens believe they need financial knowledge and skills to achieve their life goals, and 94% of parents agree.* Yet teens score an average of 64% on the National Financial Literacy Test, revealing a significant gap between ambition and preparation. Parents rank personal finance as the #1 most difficult life skill to teach their children, with 81% saying they wish they had more tools and resources to help.** Greenlight offers a debit card and app that teaches kids and teens how to earn, save, give, and spend wisely — all with parental oversight. Using the Greenlight app, parents can quickly send money, automate allowance payments, manage chores, set flexible spending controls, and receive real-time notifications of all transactions. Kids gain hands-on money management experience alongside access to Greenlight Level Up™, an in-app financial literacy game featuring a best-in-class curriculum, educational challenges, and rewards. “As a community bank, we’re invested in our customers’ futures — and that includes their kids. We know parents want to teach their children good money habits, but it’s not always easy to know where to start. Greenlight gives families a real, hands-on way to do that together, and we’re proud to make it available to our customers at no cost. If we can help a child in our community grow up feeling confident about money, that’s a win for all of us.” — Laura Smith, Chief Retail Banking Officer, Great Southern Bank Great Southern customers can receive a free* Greenlight subscription by visiting greenlight.com/greatsouthern and connecting their Great Southern account as a funding source. Customers who already have an existing Greenlight account can also transition to the Great Southern partnership program by adding their Great Southern account as a funding source and contacting Greenlight customer service. More than 7 million parents and kids already use Greenlight to manage money together. Greenlight has been named the top debit card for kids and teens by the Wall Street Journal and is trusted by families nationwide. About Great Southern Bank Headquartered in Springfield, Mo., with $5.6 billion in assets, Great Southern offers a broad range of banking services to customers. The Company operates 88 retail banking centers in Missouri, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Arkansas and Nebraska: commercial lending offices in Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Omaha, and Phoenix, and one Home Loan Center in Springfield. The common stock of Great Southern Bancorp, Inc., is listed on the Nasdaq Global select Market under the symbol “GSBC.” About Greenlight Greenlight Financial Technology, Inc. is on a mission to help parents raise financially smart kids. Greenlight offers a debit card and app designed for families, with tools that help kids earn, save, give, spend wisely, and invest — all under parental supervision. For more information, visit greenlight.com . Greenlight is a financial technology company, not a bank. The Greenlight app facilitates banking services through Community Federal Savings Bank (CFSB), Member FDIC. *Great Southern Bank customers are eligible for the Greenlight SELECT plan at no cost when they connect their Great Southern Bank account as the Greenlight funding source for the entirety of the promotion. Subject to minimum balance requirements and identity verification. Upgrades will result in additional fees. Upon termination of promotion, customers will be responsible for associated monthly fees. See terms at https://greenlight.com/promotionsgeneralterms for details. Offer ends 5/3/2029. Offer subject to change and partner participation. **Survey insights were collected by Greenlight through a Researchscape survey fielded between March 22–24, 2024, among 2,310 respondents in the U.S., split between kids and teens ages 10–19 and parents of 10–19 year olds. ***Survey insights were collected by Greenlight through a Researchscape survey fielded between February 9–12, 2023, among 1,034 U.S. respondents, all of whom were working parents of 8–18 year olds.

title: 50 Best Trade Show Giveaways, Conference Swag & Event Giveaway Ideas (2026)
summary: Discover 50 of the best trade show giveaways, conference swag and event giveaway ideas for every budget, from affordable branded items to VIP gifts.
body_text: Trade show giveaways are branded promotional products businesses hand out at conferences, expos, and corporate events to attract booth visitors, generate leads, and increase brand awareness. From inexpensive event giveaways to premium corporate event giveaways, the right promotional products help your company stand out long after the event ends. In this guide, we've rounded up 50 of the best trade show giveaways, conference giveaways, and trade show swag ideas for every budget. ‍ Best Trade Show Giveaways Under $10 The best trade show giveaways don’t have to come with a big price tag. Affordable items under $10 are ideal for attracting booth visitors, reaching a large number of attendees, and keeping your brand visible long after the event. From everyday essentials to useful branded accessories, these budget-friendly trade show giveaways offer plenty of opportunities to customize products with your company logo, colors and messaging. ‍ Pens: A classic trade show giveaway for a reason. Pens are affordable, practical, and easy to distribute in large quantities. Customize them with your logo or brand colors for an everyday item attendees can use long after the event. Shown: Jotter Pen ‍ Stickers: Branded stickers give attendees an easy way to personalize laptops, water bottles, notebooks, and other everyday items. Choose a creative design people will actually want to use and show off. Photo courtesy of A24 Films ‍ Patches: Branded patches offer a more distinctive alternative to traditional promotional products. Custom designs can showcase your logo, artwork, or event messaging while giving attendees something collectible and easy to take home. Photo courtesy of GMTRY (left) and River City Leather Co (right) ‍ Hand Sanitizer: A practical choice for busy conferences and trade shows, portable hand sanitizer is an event essential that attendees will appreciate. Customize the packaging with your branding for a useful giveaway that’s easy to carry. Shown: Noshinku® Hand Sanitizer ‍ Sharpie Markers: A branded Sharpie is an unexpected upgrade from the standard promotional pen. Useful at home, at work and on the go, it’s a recognizable everyday item that can keep your brand within reach. Photo courtesy of Aimé Leon Dore (left) and Only NY (right) ‍ Notebooks: Custom notebooks give attendees a convenient place to jot down session notes, ideas, and new contacts throughout the event. Add your logo or custom artwork to create a practical giveaway with plenty of staying power. Shown: Doodle Connect Vegan Leather Notebook ‍ Pint Cups: Reusable pint cups are a versatile option for trade shows, company events, and networking happy hours. Customize them with your logo or event artwork for a giveaway attendees can continue using at home. Shown: ETS Express Pint Cup ‍ Lip Balm: Custom Lip balms are lightweight, easy to distribute, and especially well-suited for outdoor events, festivals, and casual networking experiences. Funi colors and custom graphics can turn a simple giveaway into memorable branded merch. Shown: Organic Lip Balm ‍ Beverage Holders: Insulated beverage holders offer a more elevated take on traditional drinkware giveaways. They help keep drinks cool while providing a useful, highly visible space for custom branding. Shown: Hang Cool Insulated Beverage Holder ‍ Calendar: Custom calendars keep your brand visible throughout the year rather than just during the event. Make the design worth displaying with original artwork, useful information, or creative branding. Shown: Vertical Academic Calendar ‍ Best Conference Giveaways for Attendees ($10–50) The best conference giveaways combine everyday usefulness with quality that attendees will appreciate. In the $10–$50 range, branded apparel, bags, drinkware and tech accessories offer more perceived value while still being practical for larger events. Choose conference swag that reflects your audience and brand to give attendees something they’ll want to use or wear long after the event ends. ‍ Pencil Cases: A custom pencil case is a compact, versatile conference giveaway that can hold pens, chargers, cosmetics, and other small essentials. Choose a stylish design that attendees can repurpose long after the event. Shown: Dayla Genuine Cowhide Pencil Case ‍ Nalgene Water Bottles: Durable, recognizable, and made for everyday use, Nalgene bottles make practical conference giveaways for active audiences. Add custom branding to create reusable drinkware attendees can carry to the office, gym, or outdoors. Photo courtesy of OnlyNY ‍ Branded Cap: A well-designed branded cap turns conference swag into something attendees may actually wear. Keep the branding thoughtful and the design versatile to extend your company’s visibility beyond the event. Shown: AsColour 6-Panel Unstructured James Cap ‍ T-shirt: Custom T-shirts are a conference swag staple with plenty of room for creative branding. Choose a quality fabric, flattering fit, and wearable design to make your event tee feel more like retail merchandise. Shown: AS Colour Classic Tee ‍ Crewneck Sweatshirt: A comfortable crewneck sweatshirt offers greater perceived value than a basic tee while remaining versatile enough for everyday wear. Subtle embroidery or a thoughtfully designed graphic can give this conference giveaway a premium feel. Photo courtesy of OnlyNY ‍ Carhartt Polo: Custom polos are a polished choice for corporate conferences, golf events, and professional audiences. Add an embroidered logo for branded apparel that transitions easily from the event to the workplace. Shown: Carhartt Force Polo Pocket ‍ Champion Unisex Raglan Tee: Raglan tees offer a sportier alternative to the standard branded T-shirt. Their distinctive sleeve design creates a casual, wearable piece of conference swag that can showcase your brand without feeling overly promotional. Photo courtesy of Champion ‍ Micro-terry Pullover Hoodie: A comfortable branded hoodie is the kind of conference giveaway attendees are likely to keep in regular rotation. Choose quality materials and understated customization to create apparel with lasting appeal. Shown: Port Authority® Microterry Pullover Hoodie ‍ Battery Pack: Portable power banks solve a real problem at conferences, where attendees rely on their phones throughout the day. A compact custom charger keeps devices powered while putting your brand on a useful tech accessory. Shown: Clutch Battery Pack ‍ Reusable Totes: A reusable tote gives attendees an immediate way to carry brochures, samples, and other event swag. A well-designed bag can continue generating brand visibility at the grocery store, gym, office, and beyond. Shown: The Standard Baggu ‍ Corporate Event Giveaways & VIP Gifts ($50+) Premium corporate event giveaways and VIP gifts are designed to make a lasting impression on high-value attendees, clients, executives, and special guests. From premium apparel and travel gear to tech and lifestyle products, gifts in the $50+ range offer greater perceived value and can be customized with your logo or branding for a memorable, elevated experience. ‍ Half-Zip Fleeces: A premium half-zip fleece combines comfort, versatility, and strong perceived value. Add subtle custom branding for a polished corporate event giveaway that recipients can wear at work, while traveling, or on the weekend. Customize it with subtle branding for a premium travel gift recipients can use for weekend trips, workouts, and more. Shown: Well Studio Recycled Nylon Duffel - AWARE™ ‍ Stanley Tumblers: Popular branded drinkware can create excitement before the event even ends. Shown: Stanley Flowstate Tumbler ‍ Turkish Cotton Towels: A premium Turkish cotton towel is an unexpected corporate event giveaway that works especially well for retreats, wellness events, and travel programs. Lightweight and versatile, custom towels are used at the beach, pool, or at home. Shown: Slowtide Turkish Towel ‍ Massage Guns: A portable massage gun delivers a wellness-focused experience that stands out from traditional event swag. It’s a memorable choice for VIPs, fitness-focused audiences and corporate wellness programs. iLive™ Massage Gun with Case ‍ Backpack Coolers: A backpack cooler combines the convenience of a hands-free bag with insulated storage for food and drinks. It’s an especially useful premium giveaway for outdoor events, company retreats and active audiences. Shown: Igloo® Marine 30 Can Backpack Cooler ‍ Bluetooth Headphones: Wireless headphones are a high-value tech gift recipients can use for work, travel, and entertainment. Choose a quality pair and thoughtful customization to create a corporate giveaway with everyday appeal. Shown: Positive Vibration Riddim On-Ear Bluetooth Headphones ‍ Quilted Full-Zip Hoodies: A quilted full-zip hoodie blends the comfort of a sweatshirt with the warmth and structure of a lightweight jacket. Premium materials and subtle branding make it a sophisticated option for VIP gifting. Shown: Marine Layer Corbet Quilted Full Zip Hoodie ‍ VIP trade show swag ideas $100+ Polaroid Cameras: A Polaroid camera turns a premium gift into an experience, giving recipients a fun way to capture and print memories instantly. It can also become part of the event itself through photo activations, branded displays or VIP experiences. Shown: Polaroid Camera ‍ Weekender Bags: A premium weekender bag is a practical gift for frequent travelers and busy professionals. Add understated branding to create a sophisticated piece recipients can use for business trips and weekend getaways. Shown: Samsonite Virtuosa Weekender ‍ Wool Throws: A high-quality wool throw brings warmth and comfort to premium corporate gifting. It’s a timeless option for VIPs, executives and top clients, especially when paired with subtle custom branding or premium packaging. Shown: Faribault Wool Trapper Throw ‍ Diffusers: A stylish diffuser brings a wellness and lifestyle element to corporate gifting. Choose a design recipients will be happy to display at home or in the office for a gift that feels personal and elevated. Shown: Vitruvi Stone Diffuser ‍ Ember Travel Mugs: An Ember Travel Mug uses smart temperature control to keep drinks at the recipient’s preferred temperature. It’s a premium tech-meets-drinkware gift that works especially well for executives, frequent travelers and coffee lovers. Shown: Ember Travel Mug ‍ 3-in-1 Wireless Chargers: A 3-in-1 wireless charger creates one convenient place to power multiple compatible devices. Its everyday usefulness and clean design make it a premium tech gift for VIP attendees and high-value prospects. Shown: Native Union 3-in-1 Qi2 Wireless Charger ‍ The North Face Jackets: Premium branded outerwear from a recognizable brand can make a strong impression on recipients. Keep the customization subtle for a versatile jacket; VIPs and clients will be more likely to wear it regularly. Shown: The North Face Venture 2 Jacket ‍ Electric Kettles: A premium electric kettle is an unexpected lifestyle gift that can elevate a recipient’s daily coffee or tea routine. Its distinctive design and everyday usefulness make it a memorable alternative to traditional corporate swag. Shown: Fellow Stagg Electric Kettle ‍ Bluetooth Charging Speakers: A premium Bluetooth speaker combines entertainment with everyday functionality, while select models can also help keep devices charged. It’s a high-impact gift for VIPs, top clients and special event experiences. Shown: Bang & Olufsen Beolit 20 ‍ Waterproof Backpacks: A premium waterproof backpack offers protection, functionality, and modern style for commuting and travel. Its clean design makes it an elevated corporate gift that can be customized without losing its retail appeal. Shown: Rains Waterproof Backpack ‍ Best Edible trade show swag ideas Edible trade show swag offers a welcome break from traditional promotional products and gives attendees something they can enjoy during the event or take home for later. From branded candy and sweet treats to savory snacks, the best edible giveaways combine great taste with creative, custom packaging that keeps your brand front and center. ‍ Dried Fruit: Individually packaged dried fruit offers a convenient snack attendees can enjoy during the event or take home for later. Custom packaging can turn a simple, better-for-you treat into a polished, branded giveaway. Shown: Sun & Swell Organic Dried Mangos ‍ Chocolate Bars: Custom chocolate bars are a crowd-pleasing giveaway that can be tailored with branded wrappers, packaging, and flavor selections. They’re easy to distribute while still offering plenty of opportunities for creative presentation. Shown: Ritual Chocolate Mid Mountain Blend ‍ Candy Gummies: Colorful, flavorful and easy to package, gummies add a playful element to your trade show giveaway strategy. Customize the packaging or choose flavors that complement your brand for a memorable edible treat. Shown: California Gummy Bears in Tangerine Tango ‍ S’mores Kits: A s’mores kit transforms a familiar treat into an interactive gifting experience. Package the ingredients together with custom branding for a fun giveaway attendees can enjoy after the event. Photo courtesy of Mojave Mallows ‍ Happy Hour-Inspired Snacks: Cocktail-inspired snacks and flavors bring the energy of happy hour to an easy-to-distribute edible gift. They’re a creative choice for networking events, hospitality brands and audiences that appreciate something unexpected. Photo courtesy of Vesper Bites ‍ Popcorn: Gourmet popcorn is a versatile event giveaway available in flavors ranging from classic to unexpected. Custom bags, tins, or boxes provide plenty of space for branding while making the snack easy to share. Photo courtesy of Eatable Popcorn ‍ Lollipops: Custom or artisan lollipops add a colorful, playful touch to a booth display while giving visitors a quick treat to enjoy on the go. Creative flavors and branded packaging can make them even more memorable. Shown: Mango Jollipop and Assorted Flavors ‍ Toffee: Premium toffee offers a more elevated alternative to everyday candy giveaways. Package it in a custom box, bag, or tin to create a polished edible gift for attendees, clients, or VIPs. Photo courtesy of B. Toffee & Treats ‍ Seasoned Nuts: Seasoned nuts provide a savory alternative to the sweet treats commonly handed out at events. Add them to healthy gift baskets or package them individually with custom branding for a thoughtful snack attendees can enjoy on the go. Shown: Rosemary & Sea Salt Pistachios ‍ Cheese Crackers: Gourmet cheese crackers make a sophisticated savory giveaway for conferences and corporate events. Pair quality ingredients with custom packaging to create an edible gift that feels more elevated than a typical snack. Shown: Rustic Bakery Savory Cheese Coins ‍ How to measure trade show & corporate event giveaways ROI The right trade show and corporate event giveaways can help generate leads, increase brand awareness, and strengthen customer relationships. To measure ROI, define your goals before the event, then track metrics such as giveaways distributed, qualified leads, QR code scans, website visits, and meetings booked. You can also calculate cost per lead by dividing your total giveaway investment by the number of qualified leads generated. ‍ For higher-value corporate event giveaways and VIP gifts, focus on outcomes such as follow-up meetings, sales opportunities, customer retention and conversions. Comparing these results with your total investment can help identify which giveaways deliver the most value. ‍ Find the Right Trade Show Giveaways for Your Next Event The best trade show giveaways do more than fill a swag bag—they create memorable brand experiences that keep your company top of mind long after the event ends. Whether you’re looking for affordable booth giveaways, useful conference swag, premium corporate event giveaways or edible treats, the right products should reflect your audience, goals and brand. ‍ Gemnote can help you source, customize, package, and deliver custom trade show giveaways for events of every size. From branded merchandise for thousands of attendees to curated VIP gifts, our team can help you create event giveaways people will actually want to keep. ‍ Frequently Asked Questions About Trade Show Giveaways What are the best trade show giveaways? The best trade show giveaways are useful, memorable, and relevant to your audience. Popular options include pens, notebooks, reusable bags, water bottles, branded apparel, portable chargers and premium tech accessories. The right choice depends on your budget, event goals, and the attendees you want to reach. ‍ What are good trade show giveaways under $1–$100? Good trade show giveaways are available at nearly every price point. Lower-cost options include stickers, pens and other small branded items, while a larger budget can cover drinkware, apparel, bags, portable chargers and premium gifts. Consider using affordable giveaways for general booth traffic and higher-value products for qualified leads, VIPs or special promotions. ‍ What are the most popular trade show giveaways? Some of the most popular trade show giveaways include branded pens, tote bags, notebooks, water bottles, T-shirts, hats, and tech accessories. Products that are practical, easy to carry, and useful after the event tend to have the greatest staying power. ‍ How much should you spend on trade show giveaways? How much you should spend depends on your audience, event size, and goals. Inexpensive giveaways under $10 can work well for high-volume distribution, while $10–$50 conference giveaways offer greater perceived value. Premium corporate event giveaways and VIP gifts may cost $50, $100, or more and are typically reserved for high-value prospects, clients, speakers, or executives. ‍ What are unique trade show giveaways that stand out? Unique trade show giveaways go beyond basic promotional products and offer something useful, unexpected, or experiential. Ideas include Polaroid cameras, massage guns, premium travel bags, wireless chargers, gourmet snacks and curated gift kits. Creative customization and packaging can also help make a familiar product feel more distinctive. ‍ What are good conference giveaways for attendees? Good conference giveaways for attendees include products they can use during the event and afterward, such as reusable totes, water bottles, notebooks, portable chargers, and branded apparel. Consider the audience, event setting, and travel requirements when choosing conference swag that will be useful and easy to take home. ‍ Can you customize trade show giveaways with your company logo? Yes. Most trade show giveaways can be customized with your company logo, brand colors, artwork, or event messaging. Depending on the product, customization options may include screen printing, embroidery, engraving, full-color printing, custom packaging, and other decoration methods.

title: Carrot launches Carrot Rx ‘Flex program’ for U.S employers to access even more cost savings
summary: Employers can now implement fertility pharmacy benefits with even more customization, maximizing access to price transparency and cost savings
body_text: Carrot, the leading global fertility and family care platform, today announced the launch of the Carrot Rx ‘Flex Program,’ a new offering to provide pharmacy benefits at lower costs through price transparency and comprehensive member support for one of the most difficult and expensive aspects of fertility treatment: daily medication injections. Now, employers can implement Carrot Rx alongside any existing fertility benefits program providing coverage for medical services — or as a standalone solution. This new program allows employers with or without Carrot benefits that cover medical services to access Carrot Rx’s price transparency, best-in-class drug discounts, and white glove support for members in all 50 states. Carrot Rx also works seamlessly alongside any other fertility program covering medical services from fertility providers. Fertility drugs through Carrot Rx are often over 50% less expensive than medications typically paired with cycle-based pricing models for IVF. This pricing advantage often equates to nearly $5,000 in savings for employers every time an employee undergoes fertility treatment. These savings can be enormous. For example, employers with three cycles of IVF coverage as part of their fertility benefits can save an additional $15,000 per employee, per year by using Carrot Rx as a complementary pharmacy solution alongside existing medical coverage. “The Carrot Rx Flex Program gives employers and members more choice and control,” said Tammy Sun, Founder & CEO of Carrot. “Medication costs are one of the biggest barriers to fertility care. By creating flexibility — including the option to pair Carrot Rx with existing programs or offer it on its own — we’re helping employers act on this policy moment to make fertility care more affordable for more people.” Carrot Rx provides transparent, direct pricing and pharmacy fulfillment designed specifically for fertility patients. Through the new Flex Program, members who wish to buy certain prescription drugs directly through the federal TrumpRx platform on a cash-pay basis will have that option – while continuing to use their Carrot benefit to cover the remaining medications required for treatment. “We designed the Carrot Rx Flex Program around one idea: that affordability and support should go hand in hand,” said Hilary Bartlett, Chief Product Officer. “If members can find a lower price on certain medications through a public discount program, they should be able to use it — and still have Carrot guiding them through their full treatment. It’s flexibility without fragmentation.”

AWS Direct Connect now supports BGP route visibility on Virtual Interfaces
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with AWS Direct Connect now supports BGP route visibility on Virtual Interfaces
body_text: AWS Direct Connect now provides Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) route visibility, allowing you to view the routes exchanged between AWS and your on-premises routers across your private, transit, and public virtual interfaces (VIFs). You can now see which routes AWS accepted from your router and which routes AWS is advertising to your router, along with their AS path and BGP community values. This visibility helps network administrators troubleshoot routing issues, verify route propagation, and monitor their hybrid network connectivity. With this feature, you can view accepted routes (routes AWS received from your router) and advertised routes (routes AWS sends to your router) directly in the Direct Connect console or programmatically using the ListVirtualInterfaceRoutes API action. Each route displays its prefix, address family, AS path, community values, and installation timestamp, giving you comprehensive insight into your routing topology. You can filter routes by prefix, AS path, community, or address family to quickly identify specific routing behaviors. This capability is particularly valuable when managing complex multi-region architectures, validating BGP policy configurations, or diagnosing unexpected traffic patterns. This feature is available in all AWS commercial Regions and the AWS China Regions (Beijing, operated by Sinnet, and Ningxia, operated by NWCD). To learn more about BGP route visibility, visit the AWS Direct Connect documentation or access the feature through the Direct Connect console .

title: TTS Latency 2026: The Production Speed Metric for Voice AI
summary: Latency is what separates a natural conversation from a phone tree. TTFA, Coval's streaming methodology, and July 2026 results. Read the benchmark.
body_text: TTS latency is the gap between when a voice agent finishes generating a response and when the user starts hearing it. Humans respond to each other in about 400 milliseconds. That is not a soft guideline. It is the threshold below which a conversation feels natural and above which something starts to feel wrong, even if you cannot name why. A pause that is slightly too long, a response that takes just a beat too much to arrive: users register it as hesitation, confusion, or incompetence, regardless of how accurate the answer is. In a voice agent pipeline, TTS is the last model before the user hears a response. By the time the text-to-speech model gets its input, the STT model has already transcribed the user’s speech and the LLM has already generated a response. Whatever time TTS takes comes on top of all of that. Across the models in Coval’s TTS benchmark, the median Time to First Audio is 519ms, well past the 400ms threshold. As of July 23, 2026, Palabra TTS v1 leads Coval’s benchmark across TTS models on latency, with a median TTFA of 103ms. Here is what that number means, how we measure it, and why it matters. Key Takeaways Humans respond in around 400ms. TTS latency is the last thing that eats into that budget before the user hears a response. Most latency benchmarks measure throughput, not streaming. Coval measures streaming only, because that is what a call center actually runs on. TTFA (Time to First Audio) is the primary TTS latency metric: how long from when the TTS model receives text to when the first audio byte arrives. As of July 23, 2026, Palabra TTS v1 leads Coval’s TTS benchmark at 103ms median TTFA. Live rankings at benchmarks.coval.ai . Table of Contents Why Latency Is the Metric Nobody Gets Right Why TTS Latency Matters More Than People Think Throughput vs. Streaming: Why Most Benchmarks Measure the Wrong Thing How Coval Measures TTS Latency: TTFA July 2026 Benchmark Results: Palabra Leads on Latency How to Evaluate TTS Latency for Your Use Case FAQ Why Latency Is the Metric Nobody Gets Right Ask a vendor for their latency numbers and you will get a figure. Ask two vendors for their latency numbers and you will get two figures measured in completely different ways under completely different conditions. Throughput, first-byte latency, end-to-end latency, real-time factor: each measures something real, but none of them are the same thing. The number that matters for a production voice agent is specific: how long does a user wait between the agent finishing its reasoning and the agent starting to speak? That number is what Coval benchmarks. Everything else is a proxy. Why TTS Latency Matters More Than People Think TTS is the last model in the pipeline before the user hears a response. That position matters. A voice agent pipeline typically looks like this: the user speaks, the STT model returns a transcript, the LLM interprets the intent and generates a response, the TTS model converts that response into audio, and the user hears it. Each of these steps takes time. The 400ms budget for a natural-feeling conversation has to be split across all of them. TTS latency comes last. By the time the TTS model receives its input, every other step has already consumed part of the budget. A slow TTS model arrives at the end of a chain that may already be close to the threshold, tipping the whole interaction over it. The inverse is also true. A fast TTS model frees time across the pipeline. When TTS returns audio quickly, the total response time stays inside the 400ms window even when earlier steps have a slower moment. The buffer that keeps conversations feeling natural is largely built by fast TTS. For a complete breakdown of end-to-end voice pipeline latency (including STT and LLM steps), see Coval’s complete voice AI latency guide . What low TTS latency buys you: Not just faster audio. More slack in the pipeline for every upstream model. Throughput vs. Streaming: Why Most Benchmarks Measure the Wrong Thing There are two distinct use cases for text-to-speech: batch generation and real-time streaming. Batch generation is what you use to produce a completed audio file: a podcast episode, a dubbed video, an audiobook chapter. You send the full text and wait for the full audio file. Speed matters, but the user is not waiting live. According to Artificial Analysis , which measures throughput as a real-time factor (seconds of audio generated per second of compute), this is the right metric for batch work. Real-time streaming is what a call center voice agent runs on. The LLM has finished generating a response and the agent needs to start speaking as quickly as possible so the conversation does not stall. Throughput tells you almost nothing useful here because the user is not waiting for a file. They are waiting to hear anything at all, and every millisecond before that first audio byte is a millisecond of silence in a live call. Coval benchmarks streaming latency only, because that is the scenario that matters for voice agents. In Coval’s benchmark, the models that lead on streaming TTFA are not consistently the same models that lead on throughput rankings. The two lists diverge. A model that achieves excellent throughput on batch generation can still feel slow and unresponsive in a live call, and using a throughput benchmark to make a streaming decision is a common and costly mistake. How Coval Measures TTS Latency: TTFA Since Coval expanded its benchmark coverage from TTS into full STT evaluation , latency has been measured alongside accuracy as a parallel evaluation dimension. For TTS, Coval uses one primary latency metric: TTFA. Time to First Audio (TTFA) TTFA measures the latency from when the TTS model receives its text input to when the first audio byte is returned. The timer starts the moment text is sent. It stops when audio begins arriving. This is the number that directly corresponds to the gap a user experiences between the end of the LLM’s processing and the start of the agent’s voice. Low TTFA means the agent starts speaking quickly. High TTFA means there is a noticeable pause before anything is heard, regardless of how good the audio sounds once it arrives. Coval reports TTFA at both median and p95. The median tells you typical behavior. The p95 tells you how bad the worst 5% of interactions are. For a call center running thousands of calls a day, a high p95 means a meaningful share of your users are experiencing that delay on every single call. What TTFA measures: How long between when the agent has something to say and when the user hears the first sound. July 2026 Benchmark Results: Palabra Leads on Latency As of July 23, 2026, Palabra TTS v1 leads Coval’s TTS benchmark on TTFA. Benchmarks refresh every 30 minutes and the live ranking is always at benchmarks.coval.ai. Model Median TTFA Palabra TTS v1 103ms TTS-2 (Inworld AI) 196ms Flash v2.5 (ElevenLabs) 202ms What the result means: At 103ms median TTFA, Palabra TTS v1 is producing its first audio byte in roughly a quarter of the 400ms human response window. That leaves substantial time for the upstream pipeline (STT and LLM) before the total response time becomes noticeable. What the gap means: The difference between first and second place is not marginal. Palabra’s 103ms is approximately half the latency of the next closest model. At that delta, users do not need a benchmark to notice. The conversation either feels natural or it does not. What the result does not mean: Latency and audio quality are separate dimensions. A model that leads on TTFA may not lead on naturalness, accuracy, or voice cloning fidelity. Before making a vendor decision on latency alone, evaluate audio quality under your specific use case conditions. For a full provider comparison, see the Coval TTS provider guide at coval.ai/blog . How to Evaluate TTS Latency for Your Use Case Step 1: Establish your latency budget. Work backwards from the 400ms target. How much time does your STT model take? How much does the LLM need? What is left for TTS? That number is your TTFA ceiling. Step 2: Look at p95, not just median. Median performance is what you see in demos. p95 is what your users experience in production. If your call center runs 10,000 calls a day, a p95 of 600ms means 500 users per day are experiencing that delay every call. In Coval’s benchmark, the spread between median and p95 TTFA varies widely across providers. Some models hold close to their median at p95; others diverge by a large margin. Step 3: Test under your actual conditions. Text length, punctuation patterns, and LLM output style all affect TTFA. A model that is fast on short clean sentences may slow down on the verbose, structured outputs common in enterprise LLM pipelines. Benchmark under conditions that match your deployment. Step 4: Test latency and quality together. The fastest model is not useful if the audio sounds unnatural or the voice does not match your brand. Both have pass/fail thresholds. For a step-by-step evaluation framework, see how to evaluate voice agents . Track your chosen model over time with Coval’s Observe . Providers ship silent infrastructure updates that affect latency. A model that leads now may not lead next month. For a framework on embedding latency checks into a continuous evaluation workflow, see Coval’s voice AI regression testing guide . FAQ What is TTFA? TTFA stands for Time to First Audio: how long from when a TTS model receives its text input to when the first audio byte is returned. It is the primary latency metric for production voice agents because it directly corresponds to the pause a user experiences between the agent finishing its response and the agent beginning to speak. Unlike latency metrics that measure full audio generation, TTFA captures only the delay before streaming audio begins, which is the number that matters in real-time conversation. Why does 400ms matter? Humans respond to each other in roughly 400 milliseconds in natural conversation. Systems that consistently exceed this threshold feel noticeably slow to users, even when those users cannot articulate why. TTS latency is the last contributor to that total: by the time the TTS model receives input, STT and LLM processing have already consumed part of the budget. A high TTFA at the end of that chain tips the whole interaction over the threshold. The 400ms figure is not a hard cutoff, but it is the practical target for a voice agent that feels responsive rather than robotic. Why does Coval benchmark streaming latency instead of throughput? Throughput measures how many seconds of audio a model can generate per second of compute (a real-time factor). A model scoring 8x throughput generates 8 seconds of audio per second of compute. That sounds fast, but a model with strong throughput can still deliver a TTFA of 900ms in a live call; the two numbers are not correlated. Throughput captures batch generation efficiency; streaming latency captures real-time responsiveness. In a live call, the user is not waiting for an audio file; they are waiting for the agent to start speaking. Coval benchmarks streaming latency because that is the scenario contact center voice agents actually run in. How often does Coval update its TTS benchmark? Every 30 minutes. Results are surfaced across 1-day, 7-day, and 30-day rolling windows. Providers ship silent infrastructure changes that shift latency rankings, sometimes overnight. Coval’s continuous refresh means a performance change is reflected in the benchmark within the same day rather than waiting for a quarterly update. Should I choose my TTS model based on latency alone? No. Latency and audio quality are separate dimensions and both have pass/fail thresholds for production. A model that is fast but sounds unnatural, clips words, or fails on your voice cloning requirements is not production-ready regardless of its TTFA. Evaluate latency and quality together. See the Coval TTS provider guide at coval.ai/blog for a cross-provider comparison on both dimensions. What is the difference between TTS latency and STT latency? TTS (text-to-speech) latency measures how quickly a model converts text into audio. STT (speech-to-text) latency measures how quickly a model converts audio into text. In a voice agent pipeline, STT runs first (transcribing the user’s speech), then LLM processing, then TTS (generating the agent’s spoken response). Both contribute to total response time, but they run at different points in the pipeline and are measured by different metrics. STT latency is measured by TTFS (Time to Final Segment); TTS latency is measured by TTFA (Time to First Audio). Coval builds testing and evaluation infrastructure for voice AI. Independent benchmarks, continuous production monitoring, and human review, for the teams accountable when agents go live. See the platform: https://coval.ai
